rows.abstract: Seeks to create and promote an active evaluation culture in government offices - guided by the National Evaluation Framework (NEPF). Proposes to create the National Policy Evaluation Council (NPEC) alongside the Program Evaluation Units (PEU) - to ensure and facilitate the proper application and execution of the NEPF; to conduct proper monitoring and safekeeping of evaluations and other research data; and to pursue the development of the institutional capacity for NPEF´s implementation. Aims to ensure the utilization, dissemination, and feedback of evaluation findings to enhance the design, planning, programming, budgeting, and implementation of public policies, strategies, programs, projects, and other interventions.

rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING THE GRANT OF DIGITAL NOMAD VISAS, PROVIDING BENEFITS AND INCENTIVES THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Seeks to institutionalize the grant of “Digital Nomad Visas” to encourage the entry of highly skilled foreign remote workers who generate income from outside the Philippines, enhancing the country´s economy, cultural exchange, and international cooperation; creates employment opportunities and fosters a dynamic digital innovation/ecosystem.
Defines “Digital Nomad” as a foreign national who performs work remotely or engages in freelancing, consultancy, or business through digital platforms, without being locally employed by a Philippine entity.
Provides that the “Digital Nomad” should not be engaged in any form of local employment or business activities that would compete with Phil. residents, among other eligibility requirements for visa application.
Proposes for the duration and renewal of stay; application requirements; exemption from local income tax; rights and privileges; and visa revocation of specified foreign nationals.
rows.status: Substituted by HB11554

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A FREE FINANCIAL EDUCATION TO OVERSEAS FILIPINO WORKERS AND THEIR FAMILIES
rows.title_short: Free O F W Financial Education Act
rows.abstract:
Mandates all OFWs, either  land-based or sea-based, to undergo mandatory continuously updated financial education or literacy training seminars as a pre-departure and post-arrival seminar in order to promote financial responsibility among OFWs and their dependents.
Provides free mandatory financial education or literacy training programs for OFWs and their families with the Department of Migrant Workers as the lead agency, in coordination with the Overseas Workers Welfare Administration (OWWA), the Department of Finance (DOF), the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP), the Department of Interior and Local Government (DILG) and all the barangays under it, and the accredited PDOS providers across the country, including the embassies or consulates, whichever may be available, in the countries of destination.

Seeks to support the existing Philippine Immigration Act and the Anti-Trafficking of Persons Act and to strengthen the country´s commitment to a more

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR FREE FREIGHT SERVICES IN THE TRANSPORTATION OF RELIEF GOODS TO CALAMITY-STRICKEN AREAS
rows.title_short: Free Transportation Act Relief Goods Act
rows.abstract:
Aims to strengthen existing mechanisms to facilitate quick responses to the demands and needs of the citizens during disasters and emergencies. 
Directs the National and Regional Logistics Cluster led by the Office of Civil Defense (OCD), in coordination with the Department of Transportation (DOTr) and in partnership with the Philippine Postal Corporation (PPC), freight companies, common carriers, private carriers, freight forwarders, and other companies providing logistic services in the Philippines to provide freight services to duly registered relief organizations in the transportation of emergency relief goods and donated articles to areas declared to be in a state of calamity by the President or by a local government unit (LGU). 
Grants common carriers, private carriers, and other logistics companies mandated to provide free freight services for the transportation of relief goods one hundred percent (100%) additional deduction from gross income of the amount of the cost incurred for the service provided, including the actual cost of salaries and allowances of personnel directly involved in transporting the relief goods.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2024-11-19, transmitted to the Senate on 2024-11-21 and received by the Senate on 2024-11-21

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR PROTECTION OF THE REMITTANCES OF OVERSEAS FILIPINO WORKERS
rows.title_short: Overseas Filipino Workers ( O F Ws ) Remittance Protection Act
rows.abstract:
Aims to protect the remittances of the OFWs against usurious interest rates and exorbitant fees charged by financial institutions and provide them and their families adequate education and training on financial literacy to ensure a source of livelihood even after their overseas employment.
Provides fifty percent (50%) discount on fees imposed by banks and non-banks financial intermediaries on OFW remittances to immediate family members.
Requires all bank and non-bank financial intermediaries offering remittance services to OFWs to post in a conspicuous place within the establishment´s premises the Philippine peso equivalent rate of the foreign currencies being transacted.
Prohibits all banks and non-bank financial intermediaries from raising their current remittance fees without prior consultation with the Department of Finance (DOF), Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP), and the Department of Migrant Workers (DMW).
Imposes penalties and fines for the violation of certain acts.

rows.abstract:
Addresses the issue that building construction and urban development contribute to the world´s greenhouse gas emissions and energy consumption. Seeks to adopt sustainable practices in the construction of buildings by proposing a code and rating system that shall provide incentives to those who adopt sustainable practices to mitigate the effects of global warming.

Describes Green Building as follows: increasing the efficiency with which buildings and their sites use energy, water, and materials, reducing impacts on the environment and human health; promotion and practice of sustainable site development; improvement of indoor air quality; use of efficient energy; improvement of water management; utilization of green materials; and the preservation of cultural heritage; a building whose design, construction, renovation is both resource-efficient and ecologically efficient.

rows.title_short: Employment Opportunities For Senior Citizens And Private Entities' Incentives Act
rows.abstract:
Aims to provide available job opportunities to senior citizens who have the qualifications, capacity, and interest to be employed.
Provides private entities who shall employ senior with an additional deduction from their gross income equivalent to twenty-five percent (25%) of the total amount paid as salaries and wages, benefits, and trainings provided to senior citizens subject to the provision of Section 34 of the NIRC, as amended.
Mandates the Department of Labor and Employment, in coordination with Technical Education and Skills Development Authority (TESDA), Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) and the Civil Service Commission (CSC) to assess, design, implement, monitor and evaluate training programs that provide skills and welfare or livelihood support for senior citizens.
Directs all government agencies and instrumentalities, including government-owned and controlled corporations, local government units, and government hospitals to waive fees and charges from senior citizen jobseekers such as police clearance certificate, NBI clearance, barangay clearance, medical certificate from a public hospital, birth certificate, marriage certificate, proofs of identification, and other documents issued by the government that may be required  by employers from job applicant.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2024-11-19, transmitted to the Senate on 2024-11-21 and received by the Senate on 2024-11-21

rows.title_full: AN ACT CLASSIFYING AND PENALIZING EXTRAJUDICIAL KILLING AS A HEINOUS CRIME, PROVIDING REPARATION FOR THE VICTIMS, AND STRENGTHENING THE MECHANISM FOR ITS PREVENTION
rows.abstract:
Seeks to classify and penalize extrajudicial killings as a heinous crime, ensuring that any individual, regardless of rank or position, who is found guilty of participating in, authorizing, or condoning such acts will face appropriate criminal penalties.	

Defines EJK as any killing other than that imposed by the State pursuant to the provisions of the Constitution on heinous crimes or a deliberate and arbitrary killing of any person not authorized by a previous judgment pronounced by a competent court affording all the judicial guarantees which are recognized as indispensable by civilized peoples.Â  It may be committed by a public officer, person in authority, agent of a person in authority, or any person who is acting under the actual or apparent authority of the State (killing of individuals without judicial proceedings or legal authority)

Aims to strengthen the legal framework for investigating, prosecuting, and punishing those responsible for these heinous acts and proposes to create the EJK Claims Board which aims to provide reparations to victims of EJK and create mechanisms to address, investigate and prevent cases of EJK.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2024-11-04

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING ALL FORMS OF OFFSHORE GAMING OPERATIONS IN THE COUNTRY AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATION THEREOF
rows.abstract:
Refers “offshore gaming operation” to the offer or conduct of online games of chance or sports betting through the internet using a network and software program exclusively to offshore players or players located outside the Philippines.

Enumerates and describes prohibited acts related to the offer or conduct of any offshore gaming operation in the country.

Declares canceled - all visas and alien employment permits issued to foreign workers employed by POGOs.Â  Seeks to prohibit the Bureau of Immigration from processing visas and alien employment permits.

Provides for the liability of public officials and employees found guilty of prohibited acts related to POGOs; and for the forfeiture and confiscation of properties in favor of the government, whether they are used directly or indirectly in violation of this Act.Â

rows.author: F057;
rows.title_full: AN ACT EXPANDING THE COVERAGE OF ESPIONAGE, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE COMMONWEALTH ACT NUMBER 616 OR THE ANTI-ESPIONAGE LAW AND ARTICLE 117 OF THE REVISED PENAL CODE, AND PROVIDING HIGHER PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS THEREOF
rows.abstract:
Proposes to amend laws on espionage to make them adapt to the current situation in light of evolving global security threats, technological advancements, and the changing nature of espionage activities.

Seeks to address numerous threats from foreign intelligence services, terrorist organizations, and cybercriminals through comprehensive protection against espionage and related offenses.

Refers “NATIONAL SECURITY” as human & political security; health security; economic & financial security; food & water security; military & border security; socio-cultural security; environment & disaster security; energy security; maritime & airspace security; international security; informational & cyber security; transportation and port security.

Defines “CLASSIFIED MATTER AND/OR INFORMATION” to include everything regardless of its physical character or electronic form, classified as “top secret”, “secret”, “confidential”, and “restricted”. . . documents, equipment, projects, books, reports . . .Â  and all other products or substances that fall within the general term “matter”. Information transmitted orally is considered a “matter” for security purposes.

Amends provisions to punishable acts with their corresponding penal provisions

rows.author: F057;
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 10625 OR THE PHILIPPINE STATISTICAL ACT OF 2013, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Proposes the conversion of the PSA into the Philippine Statistics Commission to enhance the effectiveness and credibility of the national statistical system - to reinforce its independence for faster decision-making processes.

States that “THE PHILSTATSCOM SHALL HAVE THE SAME STATUS AS THAT OF A GOVERNMENTAL REGULATORY NATIONAL AGENCY ATTACHED TO THE OFFICE OF THE PRESIDENT WITH THE CHAIRMAN THEREOF BEING OF THE SAME LEVEL AS DEPARTMENT UNDERSECRETARY AND THE COMMISSIONERS THAT OF DEPARTMENT ASSISTANT SECRETARIES."

Provides for the composition of the Board; qualifications; compensation, benefits, and privileges of the Chairman and the Commissioners; and proposes that there shall be an Executive Director to be known as the National Statistician who is a citizen of the Republic of the Philippines.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ECONOMIC AFFAIRS since 2024-11-05

rows.title_full:
AN ACT AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 11223, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE
“UNIVERSAL HEALTH CARE ACT”
rows.abstract:
Tasks the Health Technology Assessment Council to review and assess the amount for each benefit package and for the PhilHealth Board to adjust income thresholds based on health funding needs. 

Seeks to amend provisions regarding missed contributions´ interest and premium contributions, schedule of self-employed direct/self-earning contributors, and professional practitioners. 

Proposes that migrant workers´ premium contributions shall based on the income floor, with 50% of their contributions subsidized by the national government. Provides that unpaid contributions not be collected upon the return of distressed migrant workers. 

States that the President may suspend premium contribution increases in case of a national emergency, public health emergency, or state of calamity.
rows.status: Substituted by HB11357

rows.author: K117;
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE INDIGENCY IDENTIFICATION SYSTEM
rows.abstract:
Seeks to provide an efficient and accessible ID system to identify and verify indigent individuals - to ensure equitable access to essential government services, social protection programs, and benefits intended.

Authorizes DSWD to determine the qualifications and criteria to categorize an indigent Filipino and establishes specific required documents to prove their status.

Proposes functional uses of Indigency ID card in all transactions requiring the identity, status, birth, and all other personal circumstances (social services, passport, and driver´s license, GSIS, SSS, PhilHealth, HDMF services and benefits, NBI, courts, prosecutor and police clearances, learning institutions admission, employment purposes, senior citizens benefits and privileges, banking and financial institutions, voting identification, etc.)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on POPULATION AND FAMILY RELATIONS since 2024-11-05

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING ARTICLE 117 OF ACT NO. 3815, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE `REVISED PENAL CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES´, AS AMENDED, PUNISHING CONSPIRACY AND PROPOSAL TO COMMIT ESPIONAGE AND MISPRISION OF ESPIONAGE, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Proposes the penalty of RECLUSION TEMPORAL AND A FINE NOT EXCEEDING FIVE MILLION PESOS . . . NOR LESS THAN THREE MILLION PESOS . . . shall be IMPOSED upon any person who:Â  
1. . . . AIDS OR INDUCES ANOTHER TO ENTER a warship, fort, or naval or military establishment or reservation or FACILITY OR CAMP OR INSTALLATION, to obtain any information, plans, photographs, or other data WHETHER of confidential nature OR NOT relative to the defense or SECURITY of the Philippine Archipelago, OR TO MILITARY TRAINING OR EQUIPMENT OF THE AFP; or

2. Being in possession, by reason of the public office he/SHE holds, of the articles, data, or information . . . , discloses their contents to . . . FOREIGN NATIONAL OR TO CRIMINAL SYNDICATES OR ELEMENTS TO THE INJURY OF THE PHILS . . . OR TO THE ADVANTAGE OF A FOREIGN NATION, . . .; OR

3. OBTAINS, RECEIVES, GATHERS, PASSES, OR CAUSES TO BE OBTAINED . . . , OR ATTEMPTS TO OBTAIN, . . . , IN ANY PLACE IN THE PHILS. INFORMATION OR DATA CONCERNING ANY VESSEL, AIRCRAFT, NAVAL STATION, MILITARY CAMP OR INSTALLATIONS OR FACILITIES, WORK OF DEFENSE, . . . OR OTHER INFORMATION OR DATA CONNECTED WITH OR RELATIVE TO NATIONAL DEFENSE OR SECURITY FOR THE PURPOSE OF DISCLOSING SUCH . . . TO A FOREIGN NATION OR ITS REPRESENTATIVE, . . . ; OR

4. LAWFULLY OR UNLAWFULLY HAVING POSSESSION OF THE INFORMATION OR DATA . . . WILFULLY COMMUNICATES, TRANSMITS OR ATTEMPTS TO COMMUNICATES . . . THE SAME TO ANY PERSON NOT ENTITLED TO RECEIVE IT.
